equation_request.abstract: We describe two quantum algorithms to approximate the mean value of a black-box function. The first algorithm is novel and asymptotically optimal while the second is a variation on an earlier algorithm due to Aharonov. Both algorithms have their own strengths and caveats and may be relevant in different contexts. We then propose a new algorithm for approximating the median of a set of points over an arbitrary distance function.

specification.problem: Approximate the mean value of a black-box function f over N inputs on a quantum computer; the abstract also mentions a median-approximation algorithm over an arbitrary distance function, but gives no details.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Only a generic textbook baseline for mean estimation on a tiny instance: amplitude estimation of the acceptance probability, which equals the mean for f with values in [0,1]. The abstract's novel optimal algorithm, the Aharonov-variant algorithm, and the median algorithm are outside this scope and not reconstructed.

equations.label: Mean value
equations.abstract_quote: approximate the mean value of a black-box function
equations.justification: Standard definition of the mean value of f over a finite domain; the abstract does not state the domain or range.
assumptions: Finite uniform domain of size N

equations.label: State preparation oracle
equations.description: Encodes f(x) in the amplitude of a flag qubit
equations.justification: Proposed standard construction; the paper's actual oracle model is unknown.
assumptions: Controlled rotation by angle 2arcsin sqrt(f(x)) is available through the oracle

equations.label: Success probability equals mean
equations.justification: Follows from eq_2 by direct computation.

equations.label: Grover iterate eigenphases
equations.latex: Q=-A S_0 A^{\dagger} S_{\chi},\quad Q\text{ has eigenvalues }e^{\pm 2i\theta}
equations.description: Amplitude-estimation operator whose phase encodes theta
assumptions: S_chi flips the sign of flag=1
S_0 flips the sign of the all-zero state

equations.label: Error bound of amplitude estimation
equations.description: Standard error bound with O(1/epsilon) uses of A, success probability at least 8/pi^2
equations.justification: Textbook amplitude estimation result, not the paper's claimed result.

registers.name: phase
registers.role: phase estimation register for amplitude estimation

specification.initial_state: All-zero state |0>^m |0>^n |0>; assumed tiny instance n=2, N=4, f values chosen by the user.

steps.description: Prepare uniform superposition over x and rotate the flag by f(x) using the oracle to form A|0>.
Apply Hadamards on the phase register, controlled powers Q^(2^j), and the inverse QFT.
Measure the phase register to get y and estimate the mean.

specification.measurement: Measure the phase register in the computational basis, giving integer y in {0,...,2^m-1}.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compute tilde mu = sin^2(pi y / 2^m); this is an approximation to mu within the bound in eq_5, not an exact equality.
assumptions: Generic amplitude estimation is used as a baseline since the abstract gives no algorithm details
f values in [0,1] with an amplitude-encoding oracle
